newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SOCCER - POLICE BRACE FOR AJAX-FEYENOORD CLASH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER - POLICE BRACE FOR AJAX-FEYENOORD CLASH.

text.p: Police said on Monday they were well prepared for possible crowd violence at next Sunday's match between Ajax and Feyenoord and did not plan any extra measures after violent clashes between the rival supporters at the weekend.

"We are not changing our security plans. We had already decided to have some 400 uniformed policemen ready to intervene if needed. Plain-clothes police will also be mingling with the crowd," Amsterdam police spokesman Klaas Wilting said.
Wilting said supporters would be filmed both inside and outside the stadium to identify trouble-makers, but that this measure had already been planned too.
Ajax and Feyenoord fans armed with weapons including knives, sticks, clubs and pickaxe handles clashed on Sunday on a road just north of Amsterdam.
Police said they were able to intervene and disperse the rival groups before matters got out of hand, adding that the gangs appeared to have arranged in advance to meet for a fight.
The violence came on the first weekend of domestic competition after the winter break on a day when Ajax and Feyenoord were playing in different parts of the country.
Feyenoord were away to Volendam, some 15 kilometres north of Amsterdam, while Ajax travelled to Graafschap Doetinchem in the east of the country.
The top-selling Dutch newspaper De Telegraaf splashed the incident across its front page on Monday under the headline "Hooligan-war by appointment."
A condemnatory editorial inside the same newspaper was simply entitled "Sickening".

At the previous match between Feyenoord and Ajax in Rotterdam last November, Feyenoord fans lobbed fire-bombs at the police and bombarded the Ajax team bus. At the time, one paper labelled the Ajax-Feyenoord fixture "the match of hate".
